reason: A moves through four sharply scened episodes — the fall of Bari, a dawn cattle raid, Urban at Clermont, the sack of Constantinople — and closes on Smithfield with a near-cinematic scene of Tyler, Walworth's blow, and a fourteen-year-old king riding at the crowd, which is the kind of writing a general reader keeps turning pages for. B is dense, analytically strong but flatter: long undifferentiated paragraphs about Zengi, Baghdad, and religious-legal instruments, with an epigraph that has nothing to do with the chapter. B also restates its core thesis (conquest must preserve a tax base; violence needs offices) at least four or five times in slightly different words, especially across the Baghdad section, whereas A varies its register and lets each episode advance the argument rather than repeat it.
